nt: The implied “you” in the imperative **hide** is feminine singular, even though the terms **your** and **you** and the implied “you” in the imperatives **Go** and **enter** are masculine singular to agree with the term **people**. It seems that when he uses a feminine form of “hide,” Isaiah is alluding to the image in verses 17 and 18 of the nation as a woman giving birth. So use the feminine form for this imperative if your language marks that distinction.

Isaiah is speaking of **fury** as if it were a living thing that could **pass by** a place. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the fury is over]

x.ASV: For, behold, Jehovah cometh forth out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.
x.Darby: For behold, Jehovah cometh out of his place to visit the iniquity of the inhabitants of the earth upon them; and the earth shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.
x.KJV: For, behold, the Lord cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.
x.YLT: For, lo, Jehovah is coming out of His place, To charge the iniquity of the inhabitant of the earth upon him, And revealed hath the earth her blood, Nor doth she cover any more her slain!'

nt: Isaiah is using **behold Yahweh, coming out** as a common expression of the culture to mean “Yahweh is about to come out.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh is about to come out]
Here, **to visit the iniquity** marks punishing the earth’s inhabitants as the purpose of Yahweh **coming out from his place**. Alternate translation: [coming to earth to punish]

Here, **his place** represents heaven, where Yahweh dwells. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from his dwelling in heaven]

Isaiah is using **visit** as a common expression of the culture to mean “punish.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to bring punishment on]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the evil deeds of]

Isaiah is speaking of **the earth** as if it were a living thing that could **uncover** hidden blood. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the blood shed on it will be revealed]

Here, **its blood** represents the evidence of violent deaths that have occurred on the earth. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the evidence of those who were murdered on it]

Isaiah is speaking of **the earth** as if it were a living thing that could deliberately **cover over its slain** to hide them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the murdered will no longer be hidden]
